## 4 · Unresolved decisions — **all of them**

### Canon and custody

**`U-01` · Which candidate explanation is true — HELD FOR CHAIRMAN**
Eleven live candidates, none confirmed, none eliminated
(`OBJECTS-AND-CUSTODY.md` §7). By instruction the mystery is not solved in this
bible. Every candidate is written so that it can still be chosen; choosing one
now would foreclose the others.
**`U-01a`** · Whether the episode ends with a **corrected record** rather than a
**recovered object**. This is the thematically stronger ending and is therefore
deliberately left unchosen.

**`U-02` · Version mark conflict — HELD**
Stored row says **`EPISODE 1 V4`**. Poster asset says **`ER·TX·001·BRAMBLE·V2`**.
Both are carried side by side. Which counter is authoritative, and whether they
count different things (development pass vs transmission card), is not inventable.

**`U-04` · Is "Bramble" a surname or a nickname?**
Recorded as surname (`BRAMBLE, Thomas E.`, adm. 1161) because the class register,
the admission register and the custody chain all need a register-form name. If
the Chairman rules it a nickname, the register entries change and the provenance
numbers stay.

**`U-11` · "Built with Kylee Jane in mind" — NOT INTERPRETED**
Carried verbatim from stored canon. Whether this denotes casting intent, a
character basis, a dedication or an audience-of-one design target is **not
guessed at** and nothing in the bible depends on a reading of it.

**`U-12` · Does WYCK use words in EP001?**
Stored canon: *"WYCK talks directly to Bramble."* EP001 instruction: WYCK
"manifests subtly as his inner questioning signal." These are compatible but not
identical. The bible sets WYCK at its quietest register (`W-1…W-6`) and **does
not write a line of WYCK dialogue**. Whether EP001 uses spoken WYCK at all is
the Chairman's call.

**`U-17` · Episode title.** Working title *Eleven Where Twelve Should Be*.

### Visual

**`U-03` · The poster seam.**
The supplied reference poster carries a curved luminous vertical seam with a
second world behind it. Under the visual transmission law (§2.3) that seam would
be a **visible dimension wall** and is prohibited **in episode frames**. The
bible treats it as **key-art language only**. Confirmation needed that key art
keeps it while episode frames do not — or that it is retired from both.

**`U-07` · School uniform in a 1945 village primary school — UNSOURCED.**
Recorded as `[S]` simulation (no uniform; ordinary mended clothes). Needs a
documented source before any costume commitment.

**`U-08` · Chalkboard manufacturer — NO EARTH PATTERN SOURCED.**
`Nadin & Slee` is pure invention, unlike the publisher and the furniture maker,
which rest on `S-14` and `S-15`. Either source a real British blackboard trade
pattern, or accept the maker as unanchored simulation.

### Historical sourcing gaps carried honestly

**`U-06` · Branch-line operating company.**
Left unfixed. Naming a pre-nationalisation main-line company for Corvesley's
branch would attach a real company to a fictional place without a sourced basis.

**`U-13` · School meals at Corvesley.**
The 1944 Act made meals and milk a statutory duty (`S-09`). The bible gives
Corvesley **no kitchen** and a container meal three days a week. The rate of
implementation in small rural schools in late 1945 is **not sourced**.

**`U-15` · Bramble's father's service and demobilisation.**
Written as "serving overseas, not yet home." The demobilisation mechanics of
late 1945 are **not sourced** and are therefore not depicted.

**`U-16` · Who pays Pearl's milk penny.**
School milk was **still charged at 1d in 1945** and did not become free until
August 1946 (`S-16`). The 1934 scheme allowed free milk to poor children **at
discretion**; how that discretion ran in 1945, and whether a billeted child
qualified, is **not sourced**.

### Chairman's core-interest thread

**`U-05` · Foregrounding the 1945 Black-Britain material.**
`SOURCES-1945.md` §3 carries, at primary-subject depth: Liverpool's Black
community from the 1730s with ten traceable generations (`S-28`); Butetown from
the 1800s with its own institutions by the 1940s (`S-29`); ~16,000 West Indian
volunteers and ~5,400 RAF arrivals June 1944–1945 (`S-30`); ~240,000
African-American servicemen and ~2,000 "brown babies" (`S-31`); and the colour
bar tested in **Constantine v Imperial Hotels Ltd [1944] KB 693** (`S-32`).

EP001 uses **one** of these in the foreground — Pearl Emanuel's documented
evacuation route (`S-26`, `S-28`) — and holds the rest as background truth.
**Whether, and in which episode, the colour bar and the "brown babies" thread
come forward is the Chairman's decision, not this build's.**

Two constraints are **not** negotiable and are recorded as findings rather than
options: the "brown babies" were born from ~1943 and are therefore **infants in
November 1945, not classmates** (`S-31`); and a Black child in a small inland
market town needs a **documented route** rather than an assertion (`S-26`).

### Operational

**`U-09` · The program identifier is asserted, not read.**
`ER-PROGRAM-BRAMBLE-WYCK` exists nowhere in the repository and could not be
checked against the backend (§1.1). If the live backend already carries a
different program identifier for this lane, this delta must be reconciled to it —
through custody, per `ER-CUSTODY-BRAMBLE-0001`'s own rule.

**`U-10` · No name clearance.**
`Corvesley`, `Hallam & Rudge Ltd`, `Bidwell & Cope`, `Nadin & Slee` and every
Corvesley shop name were **not** checked against any gazetteer, companies
register or trade-mark register. A web search returned no English settlement
called Corvesley, which is a weak negative, not a clearance.

**`U-14` · Mirror to the deployment authority?**
Per `DASHBOARD_AUTHORITY.md`, material intended for the live Chairman dashboard
must be merged into `vyc2st-ctrl/thylora-executive-dashboard` and witnessed on
`thylora-public-world`. **This delta was not mirrored** — it is development
documentation, and mirroring is a Chairman decision.
